scope: Opt-in stock relayd TCP passthrough into mandatory PROXY v1, actual companion TLS/SNI/Host admission and Coraza/CRS. Native fixture/checker/CLI compilation, unchanged legacy controls, no product adoption.

findings.authority: Matched app/api and owned ingress port pass; cross-host/wrong-port/folded/trailing-dot/unknown authority return 421 with zero effects. Empty/unknown/removed SNI fail handshake.
findings.limits: Plain HTTP after the mandatory prefix returns 400 without an effect. Bare TLS has no prefix and is rejected; slow partial TLS is server-closed within the tested budget, followed by recovery. TLS 1.0 and h2-only negotiation reject.
findings.reload: Certificate coverage is checked before route publication. Invalid uncovered replacement keeps known good; alternate activation/removal/rollback changes subsequent SNI admission. Certificate material is startup-only.
findings.sender: A direct local sender with a forged valid prefix and verified TLS reaches inspected backend (200/one effect). PROXY addresses and loopback do not authenticate the sender.
findings.comparison: The legacy permissive api-get remains 200/one effect, while the new cross-app-api is 421/zero. Earlier strict Caddy behavior is retained from its separate immutable run; Caddy was not rebuilt or reexecuted here.

attempts.native: Initial compilation deadline failure retained separately; fresh frozen signed source build/run uses predeclared 3600/2400 guest/build tooling budgets. No traffic assertion change or host fallback.
attempts.host: Initial characterization and deadline check passed; no failed TLS implementation attempt.

limitations: Bounded research only: close-only HTTP/1.1, IPv4 PROXY v1, fixed loopback ingress and synthetic .test routes. No arbitrary streaming, upgrades, HTTP/2/3 or product TLS policy.

Certificates/keys are ephemeral owned guest inputs. No automated certificate rotation/distribution, client certificates, persistent TLS connection reload/revocation or session-resumption qualification; tickets disabled.
Local sender authentication remains open and the forged-prefix effect is retained. Forwarded identity remains untrusted; no PF or privilege-policy adoption.
Two-process relayd/companion versus Caddy maintenance and measured resource/performance/soak budgets remain unqualified. No claim that a passthrough load balancer is necessary for every deployment.
CEL package-only and unimported deprecated OpenPGP module-only residuals remain adoption blockers in the separate Caddy graph. Scans do not certify the whole selected graph.

Original image/installed daemon lineage, full CRS/application tuning, certificate operations and installer/distribution obligations remain open. No live network, service enablement, release or BootWeave schema changes.
